taxonomic_note: Current Kew accepts Passiflora foetida and several varieties; Texas is included in the native range. Local San Antonio-area records require caution because introduced lookalikes are commonly confused with it.
look_here_first: Locate the conspicuous FEATHERY/STICKY THREE-BRACT CAGE just below a flower or around a developing fruit. Then inspect downy stems/leaves, coarse lobing, and odor if safely handled. Compare mature fruit texture/color carefully with introduced scarletfruit P. lanuginosa. Don't ID the local/native-concept plant using any globally labeled P. foetida photo alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Bexar is the only exact project target-zone county locked confidently in the current review.

approval_exception.reason: Learner admission is independent from native-range certification. Preserve the scientific HOLD and the San Antonio misidentification warning.

best_field_traits: strong fetid odor when foliage is rubbed
finely divided glandular involucral bracts forming a cage
white to pale flowers with purple-blue corona
green to yellow-green fruit in the native Texas concept
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The sticky finely divided bract cage plus dense hairiness and odor are stronger than flower color alone. San Antonio-area lookalikes can be introduced P. ciliata/lanuginosa-type plants.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use the bract cage, dense pubescence, odor, leaf form, and fruit together; do not accept casual San Antonio IDs without checking these characters.
